heroHeadline: Day 376: Pakistan Extends Airspace Ban to June 23 — Ceasefire Holds Amid Entrenched Bilateral Freeze
heroSubtitle: May 21, 2026: Pakistan's Airports Authority (PAA) issued a new NOTAM on May 19 extending the ban on Indian aircraft in Pakistani airspace to June 23/24, 2026 — the sixth consecutive renewal since April 2025. India's reciprocal airspace closure remains in force. The ceasefire brokered May 10, 2025 holds at Day 376 with no Line of Control kinetic incidents, but every other pillar of the bilateral relationship remains severed: mutual airspace closure, Indus Waters Treaty suspended by India (PCA's May 15 supplemental award rejected by India as 'null and void'), all direct trade suspended, no ambassadors exchanged, no active back-channel dialogue. International analysts assess structural re-escalation risk as high despite the operational ceasefire holding — citing India's 'geography or history' Army Chief warning (May 16) and ISPR's 'severe consequences' counter (May 17). The 20-member US nuclear industry delegation concluded its New Delhi visit (May 18–21). BJP silence continues on the RSS dialogue overture.
footerNote: Data sourced from Indian MEA/MOD, Pakistan ISPR/MFA, UN Security Council, SIPRI, Crisis Group, HRW, Stimson Center
